Field 1 — Geological, civil and mining engineering

Licence in Geological, Civil and Mining Engineering

Explore the resources. Build the infrastructure. Sustainably develop Africa's potential.

Combine an understanding of terrain and materials, civil engineering techniques and knowledge of the mining sector to train professionals attentive to safety, to the quality of structures and to the responsible management of natural resources. Africa possesses a considerable geological and mining heritage and major infrastructure needs: this programme targets the scientific and technical skills able to support these development projects.

Degree

Licence — 3 years, 6 semesters, 180 credits according to the working framework

Location

Bamako, Mali — Hamdallaye ACI 2000

Languages

French and English in every semester (bilingual progression, see the Pedagogy page)

Indicative annual fee

1 350 000 FCFA/year (quoted fee, written confirmation required for 2026–2027)

Quoted additional fees

Application file: 15 000 FCFA; Licence defence: 80 000 FCFA — amounts to be confirmed for 2026–2027

Contact

+223 78 14 14 88 — abs.mail1290@gmail.com

Purpose

Train higher technicians and entry-level professionals able to take part in the study of terrain, the preparation of projects and the monitoring of geological, civil and mining activities.

General objectives

  • Master the scientific fundamentals needed to study soil and materials.
  • Understand the methods of surveying, mapping, design and monitoring of structures.
  • Integrate safety, environmental and quality rules.

Specific objectives

  • Describe geological formations and interpret field data.
  • Carry out surveys and produce base maps or plans.
  • Contribute to the preparation and monitoring of civil or mining works.
  • Use specialised software when it is available and taught.

Admission requirements

Licence entry: a scientific Baccalauréat or an equivalent qualification is recommended, subject to the official admission conditions. Master's entry: a relevant Licence in geology, civil engineering, mining or a related field, an academic record and a pathway actually open.

To be confirmed before publication: disciplinary scope, software and equipment actually accessible, field trips and any professional requirements.

Teaching methods and assessment

Written tests, practical-work reports, maps/plans, case studies, field assessments, examinations, a project and an internship. Validation according to the approved institutional rules.

Targeted teaching approach: approximately 40 % theoretical input and 60 % practice, projects, tutorials, field work, internships and immersions, subject to the approved curriculum. Field trips comply with safety instructions and protective equipment defined in the curriculum.

Targeted competencies and learning outcomes

Each competency is paired with an expected learning outcome at the end of the programme.

CodeTargeted competencyExpected learning outcome
GCM01
Observe and describe terrainCollect observations and characterise materials.
GCM02
Map and measureOrganise survey data and produce a readable representation.
GCM03
Understand materials and structuresExplain the main properties and constraints.
GCM04
Contribute to technical studiesRead plans and apply calculation methods suited to the level.
GCM05
Integrate safety and environmentIdentify risks and propose prevention measures.
GCM06
Communicate resultsWrite a report and present technical data.

Licence programme structure

Licence: 3 years, 6 semesters, 180 credits according to the working academic framework. The detailed distribution of teaching units is set out in the validated semester curriculum of the field.

CycleOrganisationStatus
Licence 1Semesters 1 and 2: fundamentals, study methods and first applicationsGeneral framework of 30 credits per semester; see the detailed curricula annexed
Licence 2Semesters 3 and 4: deeper study, practice and projectsTeaching units, hourly volumes and credits according to the field's curriculum
Licence 3Semesters 5 and 6: progressive specialisation, project, internship and dissertation according to the curriculumAcademic validation according to the approved regulations

The complete semester tables (teaching units, subjects, CM/TD/TP/TPE volumes and credits) appear in the annexed pedagogical volume and must be checked and harmonised before publication as final data. The Master's curricula of the geological, civil and mining field must be validated before enrolments open.

Main courses

Public-facing list, according to the validated curriculum

  • Applied mathematics and physics
  • General chemistry and materials
  • General and structural geology
  • Mineralogy, petrography and geological mapping
  • Surveying and field surveys
  • Soil mechanics and construction materials
  • Hydrology and geotechnics according to the curriculum
  • Technical drawing and design software
  • GIS: QGIS and mapping tools according to resources
  • Introduction to professional tools: AutoCAD Civil 3D, Surpac according to availability
  • Mining operations, safety and environment
  • Scientific English, projects and field trips

Software such as QGIS, AutoCAD Civil 3D and Surpac may be used according to the teaching objectives and the equipment available.

Three connected strands

A programme at the crossroads of Earth sciences, structural engineering and mineral resources.

Geological strand

Observe and characterise terrain, interpret geological and geotechnical data, carry out mapping.

Civil engineering strand

Materials, soil mechanics, design and monitoring of structures, plans and basic calculations.

Mining strand

Exploration and exploitation of mineral resources, safety, environment and site rehabilitation.

Particular attention is paid to safety, to the responsible management of resources, to reducing environmental impacts and to taking account of the needs of communities.

End-of-module projects and defences

Field notebook, geological mapping, analysis of a material, a geotechnical case study or a mini site-monitoring project. Presentation of results and technical report.

Immersions, field trips and internships

Supervised field trips, visits to construction sites, geological sites and mining companies where agreements and safety allow; a professional internship with a supervisor and a report.

Resources available to students

Lecturers in geology, surveying, materials and civil engineering; measuring instruments, personal protective equipment, cartographic resources and software according to licences and availability. No laboratory or specific partnership is claimed without verification.

Monitoring and continuous improvement: results by teaching unit and by semester, student evaluation of teaching, follow-up of projects and internships, annual collection of feedback from graduates and employers when data are available, periodic revision of curricula and content.

Career paths and professional prospects

Indicative prospects, subject to skills, certifications and the requirements of each employer — career paths are prospects, not job guarantees:

Assistant geologist
Field technician
Assistant surveyor
Materials technician
Site assistant
Geotechnical or mining studies assistant

Relevant sectors (indicative): engineering consultancies, construction companies, mining companies, laboratories, mapping agencies, technical services and environmental and geotechnical organisations.
